title: Live STEM Imaging of Electronic Device Performance Degradation under Beta Radiation
content: A transmission electron microscope (TEM) necessarily irradiates the sample that it is imaging. The damage caused by this irradiation has been studied extensively to understand its impact on image quality [1]. But, for a couple of reasons, the TEM has seldomly been used to simultaneously produce and observe radiation-induced changes to electronic device performance. First, it is difficult to prepare electrically contacted cross section samples without destroying a device’s electronic functionality. And second, even with an ideal sample, standard TEM contrast is primarily related to physical structure and composition. It reveals little about the electronic properties that govern device function.
